findings.issue: Filter controls are uncontrolled refs synced to loader data via two effects, including a mount effect that replays pre-hydration input (same pattern at pokemon.tsx:150-153); fragile and fights the documented Form/useSearchParams approach.
findings.suggestion: Drive the controls from useSearchParams (or a debounced controlled state) and keep only one well-tested sync path; document or drop the pre-hydration replay if tests show it is unnecessary.

findings.issue: Module-level cache stores expired entries forever (they are only overwritten on next access), so memory is bounded only by the API's resource space.
findings.suggestion: Sweep expired entries on insert or cap the map size (e.g., LRU); at minimum note the bound relies on the fixed API snapshot.

findings.issue: isbot and @react-router/node are declared but never imported; the default entries don't need them.
"<n> of 6" hardcodes the team size that TEAM_SIZE already defines.
findings.suggestion: Render `members.length} of {TEAM_SIZE}` and keep the constant as the single source.

findings.issue: Row key appends the array index ("name-level-i"), which can cause needless remounts if rows reorder after sorting.
findings.suggestion: Key by name plus level (and method when needed), which is unique within a table.

findings.issue: The catch-all route's default component renders null and is effectively dead code; the 404 UI lives in root.tsx's ErrorBoundary via the exported NotFound helper.
findings.suggestion: Render the NotFound UI directly in this component (or delete the null component) so the 404 flow has one home.

findings.issue: versionGroupOrders() rebuilds its Map on every Pokémon page load, relying on the per-URL cache instead of caching the assembled result like getIndex does.
findings.suggestion: Wrap it in the same cached() helper under a stable key.

summary: A clean, current-idiom React Router v8 framework-mode app: typed loaders, data() 404s, SSR with a cookie-fed root loader that makes the team feature flash-free, and a well-bounded server-only data layer. The only real design conversation is the hand-rolled filter-control synchronization in home.tsx, which a reviewer should understand before approving. I'd merge after one round of nits.
